ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$, $\angle BAD=70^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle BCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in circle O, $\angle$BAD=$70^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle$BAD+$\angle$BCD=$180^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle$BCD=$\boxed{110^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, points A, B, C, and D are all on the circumference, and line segments AB, BC, CD, and DA connect to form the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD; A is on the left side, B is on the lower right side, C is on the upper right side, D is on the upper left side, and O is marked inside the circle. ∠BAD is the angle at vertex A formed by BA and DA, and ∠BCD is the angle at vertex C formed by BC and DC; they are a pair of opposite angles of this cyclic quadrilateral. Reasoning: The problem gives ∠BAD = 70°. The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, so ∠BAD + ∠BCD = 180°. Therefore ∠BCD = 180° - 70° = 110°.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: points A, B, C, and D lie on the same circle, with segments AB, BC, CD, and DA forming an inscribed quadrilateral; angle BAD is the angle at A and angle BCD is the opposite angle at C. From the text, take the given measure ∠BAD = 70°. Use the cyclic quadrilateral theorem that opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral are supplementary: ∠BAD + ∠BCD = 180°. Therefore compute ∠BCD = 180° − 70° = 110°.
